messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testEncodingOutputStream` verifies that the encoding is properly passed to various ArchiveOutputStream implementations created by the ArchiveStreamFactory. The test iterates over multiple test cases and checks if the encoding expected matches the encoding actually set in the output stream created by the factory method.

From the code of `getOutputStreamFor` used in the test, it simply calls `createArchiveOutputStream` on the ArchiveStreamFactory passing the archiver type and a ByteArrayOutputStream.

Inspecting the `createArchiveOutputStream` method shows that for some archive formats (like Zip and Tar), the encoding (`entryEncoding`) is passed to the constructor or set on the stream. For instance:
- ZipArchiveOutputStream has `setEncoding(entryEncoding)` if encoding is set.
- TarArchiveOutputStream uses `new TarArchiveOutputStream(out, entryEncoding)` if encoding is set.
- CpioArchiveOutputStream also uses encoding when set.

However, for other archive formats (notably `JarArchiveOutputStream` returned at line 297), the encoding is not passed or set at all. It just calls `new JarArchiveOutputStream(out)` without considering `entryEncoding`.

This matches the bug report that says "ArchiveStreamFactory fails to pass on the encoding when creating some streams" including `JarArchiveOutputStream` and others like Arj, Cpio, Dump that are apparently missing encoding propagation.

Similarly, in the `createArchiveInputStream` method (not directly tested here, but from the bug report description), many archive stream implementations do have encoding passed if `entryEncoding` is set (Arj, Cpio, Dump, Jar etc.) but some others might not.

The core of the issue is that some ArchiveOutputStream and ArchiveInputStream implementations do not receive the encoding parameter in their constructors or setter methods when created by ArchiveStreamFactory, leading to encoding mismatches and thus test failures when encoding is expected to be honored.

The recent bug report mentioning that encoding support was added in a way that broke immutability/thread-safety indicates that encoding handling was introduced in stages and may be inconsistent across formats.

In summary:
- The test fails because when ArchiveStreamFactory creates some streams (especially JarArchiveOutputStream and others), it does not pass the encoding to the constructors or via setters.
- The code shows explicit encoding handling only for some archive types but not all that support encoding.
- This causes the encoding expected in tests to not match the actual stream encoding, leading to the test failure.
- The current bug report confirms that the problem affects Arj, Cpio, Dump, Jar (both InputStream and OutputStream variants).

Hence, the root cause is missing propagation of the encoding parameter to all relevant ArchiveStream implementations created in ArchiveStreamFactory methods.

Next, I will identify methods that should be fixed to add consistent encoding parameter passing.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveOutputStream(java.lang.String, java.io.OutputStream)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(java.lang.String, java.io.InputStream)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
